After the death of Qutub-ud-din Aibak in 1210, Aram Shah ascended the throne of the Delhi Sultanate [d2][d3]. According to Wikipedia's article on Aram Shah, Aibak died unexpectedly in Lahore during a sport game without having named a successor, and the Turkic nobles in Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor [d2]. Aram Shah ruled for only a brief period — approximately eight months — before being defeated by Iltutmish [d1][d9]. Iltutmish, a former slave and son-in-law of Aibak, was invited by a group of nobles to occupy the throne, marched to Delhi, seized power, and later defeated Aram Shah's forces at Bagh-i Jud [d2][d3].
